div.head: ECf 35.1 A 2
div.ab: Princeps uero Albanie duxit eam in uxorem casu fortuito. Picti enim Albanie a Picto† duce uocantur, Scotti uero Albanie a Scotto duce nuncupantur. Est enim Albania pars†† monarchie regni huius, quod olim uocabatur regnum Britannie. Dicuntur enim et uocantur Britones a Bruto rege, qui Troianus fuit, ex quo regnum uniuersum nomen suscepit. Britones enim quasi Bruti Troiani sunt; et uenerunt et exierunt olim a Troia magna.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 664 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page.

This passage is not part of ECf or ECf retr: it is one of the additions of the London collection (Leges Anglorum s. XIII in. Londoniis collectae), which Liebermann prints across the page after ECf 35, 1 as an insertion into ECf retr. 35, 1 (35, 1 A). The dictionary cites it as “ECf 35,1 A …”, so it is kept with ECf here.
The dagger after “Picto” and the double dagger after “pars” refer to Liebermann’s marginal references: † Galf. Mon. VI 5, †† I 16 (Geoffrey of Monmouth).
Liebermann prints his note 12 (“fehlt Ld”) three times in this passage.
